sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal-State; common law in Alberta under the Federal-State doctrine; bijural federal system with Quebec civil law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.31 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control); Alberta Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9 (ISC Register provisions); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 20; FINTRAC regulations and guidance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (ISC registers are maintained confidentially; accessible to FINTRAC, CRA, law enforcement, and specified corporate constituents; not publicly searchable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status from the foreign corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization via Global Affairs Canada if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the Canadian entity and appointing directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction notary public / board of directors

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney to resident incorporator or registered agent
Certified true copy of Memorandum / Articles of Association of the ultimate parent or foreign shareholder
Passport and proof-of-address of each director, UBO, and authorized signatory (certified copies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority; bank or utility provider; notarized certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against Canada's domestic sanctions lists (SEMA, United Nations Act, Magnitsky listings), OFAC SDN List (for USD payment rails), European Union and United Kingdom consolidated lists, and intergovernmental FATF watchlists; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) of domestic or foreign origin; FINTRAC reporting of suspicious transactions and terrorist property; risk-tiering of the shipyard as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under the commercial maritime sector.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada); Provincial: Alberta Corporate Registry Online (Corporate Registry, Government of Alberta)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English and/or French; names in a non-Roman script require certified transliteration into English or French; Alberta requires a distinctive element plus a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'); the CBCA prohibits names that are contrary to public policy, misleading, or confusingly similar to existing registered or reserved names per the NUANS report.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is refused by the Alberta Director of Corporate Registry or by Corporations Canada, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the issuing authority within 30 days, submitting a new NUANS report, evidence of consent from any party whose name is referenced, and a revised proposed name; an unsuccessful reconsideration may be appealed to the provincial Court of King's Bench in Alberta under the Business Corporations Act or to the Federal Court for CBCA corporations; a fresh 90-day name reservation must precede any re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is tolerated solely as a registered-office service address in Alberta provided a physical street address is maintained by a licensed registered agent for service of process; however, for a commercial shipyard (ISIC 3011), lenders, Transport Canada, Export Development Canada, and the CRA generally demand real operational premises, so a pure virtual-office structure risks denial of permits, GST/HST registration, and bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 70-85% probability of unannounced on-site inspection of shipyard premises by Transport Canada, provincial occupational health and safety officers, and municipal fire/engineering authorities once operational; low (<5%) for the registered office itself if served by a reputable corporate agent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and name reservation report (federal and Alberta)
Alberta extra-provincial registration / provincial incorporation filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Alberta corporate agency or law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate minute book, common seal, organizational resolutions, and by-laws
UBO (individuals with significant control) register preparation and initial filing
Notarization and Hague Apostille authentication of foreign corporate documents (set of five instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary; Global Affairs Canada / designated provincial competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff and prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English/French translation and transliteration of foreign-script documents
PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening of directors and UBOs with FINTRAC-compliant verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT due diligence vendor / law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Transport Canada maritime sector licence pre-screening consultation
Alberta annual return and federal annual return filing (year 1)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (federal annual return is free online)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 6-22 (incorporation), s 14 and Form 1 (articles), s 18 (certificate of incorporation), s 23 (first directors), ss 102-122 (directors and officers). A federal incorporation alternative exists under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 if a federally registered corporation is preferred due to the international maritime client base. Statutory filing fee: CAD 250 (approx USD 185).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Companies and Business Registries Division), Office of the Registrar of Companies, Edmonton, Alberta.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Notice of Registered Office (Form 2), submitted electronically through the Alberta Corporate Registry Access (ACROSS) / RegistryX online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). The articles must specify the authorized share structure, and shares may be issued with or without par value; any par value shares must be fully paid before issuance. No statutory escrow account is mandated for incorporation. However, the commercial model (maritime installment payments and letter of credit) contemplates contractual escrow and refund guarantee arrangements, which the board will formally authorize at the post-incorporation organizational meeting.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the initial share subscriptions recorded in the Articles of Incorporation are accepted, and the subscribed common shares are hereby allotted and issued to the initial shareholders. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry in the Notice of Registered Office is adopted and the address recorded in the corporate register. RESOLVED FURTHER: That A. Ellis is appointed Chief Executive Officer, P. Raman Chief Financial Officer, and S. Wang Corporate Secretary, with authority to open bank accounts, the maritime installment escrow account and letter-of-credit facilities, and to execute contracts for the Corporation's shipyard operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via an accredited NUANS search house or the ACROSS portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search report to verify that the proposed corporate name (e.g., 'Alberta Ocean Container Vessel Shipyard Inc.') is distinct from existing corporate and trademark names, particularly in the marine and shipbuilding classes. Submit a name reservation request through ACROSS or instruct the search house to reserve the name for 120 days, or alternatively proceed under an Alberta numbered company designation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (no older than 90 days)
List of three proposed corporate names in priority order
Signed name request letter from the incorporator or authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as objectionable or confusingly similar, promptly submit the next alternative name in the priority list and obtain a fresh NUANS report; the Registrar may be requested to provide written reasons and reconsideration within the 120-day name reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Notice of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or Alberta-licensed legal counsel; forms prescribed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, authorized share capital and class rights, restriction on share transfers if any, number and names of first directors, and business restrictions if any. Prepare Form 2 Notice of Registered Office with the physical address in Alberta where books and records will be kept. Ensure the articles state the shipbuilding purpose as 'construction and repair of deep-sea cargo and container vessels'. Execute the articles by the incorporator with notarized signature if requested.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation (executed)
Form 2 Notice of Registered Office
Consent to act as director of each first director (Form 3)
Certificate of name reservation or confirmed numbered company designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural defect letters are cured by filing corrected articles or supplementary schedules and paying the applicable amending/refiling fee under section 19 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); the Registry issues a corrections notice describing the precise defect and the acceptable cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — online filing through ACROSS / RegistryX.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Form 1 and Form 2 electronically through an authorized corporate registry agent or the ACROSS portal, pay the CAD 250 incorporation fee, and receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation with the Alberta corporate access number. The corporation comes into existence on the date shown on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed Form 1 Articles of Incorporation
Executed Form 2 Notice of Registered Office
Consent forms of the first directors
Payment authorization for the CAD 250 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected due to payment authorization, validation, or documentation errors, the registry transaction is returned with a written rejection notice; cure by resubmitting the corrected payment authorization and schedules, with expedited re-processing available upon request within 48 hours of resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting of First Directors, Adoption of By-laws, and Ratification of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors of the corporation, acting under section 23 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); corporate minute book custodian.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the first directors or adopt a unanimous written consent resolution. Adopt the corporation's general by-laws, approve the minutes of the incorporator's meeting, ratify the execution of the Articles of Incorporation, approve the issuance of shares, appoint officers, adopt corporate seal and banking resolutions, and approve the registered office and accounting year-end.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Draft by-laws of the corporation
Consents to act as directors
Draft minutes of the incorporator's organizational meeting
First board resolution (share subscription, registered office, officers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum cannot be obtained at a physical meeting, the sole incorporator or the first director may execute a signed unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, which has the same force as a meeting resolution and cures the procedural requirement under subsection 23(2).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Share Certificates, Opening of Bank and Escrow Accounts, and FINTRAC Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; Schedule I Canadian chartered bank (e.g., RBC, TD, or BMO) in Alberta; FINTRAC regulatory obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue share certificates consistent with the subscribed share capital, record the allotment in the securities register and disclose the apposite consideration or deemed consideration. Open the operating bank account, a dedicated escrow account for maritime installment payments, and a letter-of-credit facility. Complete the bank's know-your-client procedure, including the executed board resolution, Certificate of Incorporation, register of directors, and the corporation's beneficial ownership information for FINTRAC compliance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Banking and escrow authorization resolution of the board
Register of directors and officers
Beneficial ownership and control information form
Photographic identification of directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution or FINTRAC compliance officer queries beneficial ownership or source-of-funds information, supplement the application with notarized identification documents, the corporate organizational chart, and the escrow and refund guarantee agreements; a further board resolution expressly confirming the installment escrow and LC facility may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations and Workplace Insurance Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA); Workers' Compensation Board of Alberta (WCB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the federal Business Number and the RC167 corporation income tax account. Register for GST/HST using form RC1 where annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed CAD 30,000. Register for payroll deductions using form RC15 if employees will be engaged by the shipyard. Register with Alberta TRA for provincial corporate offsetting, and enrol with WCB-Alberta for mandatory workers' compensation coverage for shipyard and fabrication workers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of registered office
Directors' names, addresses and identification particulars
Projected taxable revenue and payroll estimate for the shipyard
Corporate banking details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations are remedied by filing under the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program to relieve penalties and interest; GST/HST registration can still be completed within 30 days of incorporation without penalty if the corporation does not yet exceed the small-supplier threshold.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Shipyard Licence, Municipal Development/Building Permits and Environmental Registration Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade; municipal planning and building department of the host city; Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the post-formation licensing package: (1) municipal development permit for heavy industrial shipyard-manufacturing use and building permits for fabrication halls, berths, dry-dock and launchway structures, with P.Eng-stamped structural drawings; (2) shipyard industrial operating licence application to Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade; (3) Transport Canada vessel construction oversight request where the ships are to be registered or flagged in Canada; (4) environmental release registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA), including the air emissions and waste management plan.
required_dossiers: Zoning compliance certificate from the municipal planning authority
P.Eng-stamped structural and civil drawings for the shipyard and dry-dock
Fire safety plan and occupancy application
AEPA environmental registration form and supporting technical reports
Vessel construction specification and Canadian registry documentation
Surface wastewater and hazardous waste management plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any permit, industrial licence, or environmental registration is refused or deferred with conditions, the applicant may submit amended plans addressing the authority's written remarks, request a variance from the municipal development officer, or appeal to the applicable municipal or environmental appeal body within 21 to 30 days of the refusal letter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade — Manufacturing and Industrial Licensing Branch; with federal oversight by Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security for vessel construction standards under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipyard Manufacturing and Marine Vessel Construction Facility Licence (Alberta Major Industrial Fabrication Development Permit); Vessel Construction Oversight Approval under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 for Canadian-registered ocean container vessels.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening / Registration tier under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, Alta Reg 63/2024, together with self-administered release registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA), RSA 2000, c E-3; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not automatically required for covered dry-dock and berth fabrication activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds apply for particulate matter, VOCs and welding fume emissions under the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and the Code of Practice for Selected Air Emission Sources; wastewater discharge must meet municipal sanitary sewer by-laws and Alberta water quality guidelines; hazardous waste, used oils, paint residues and blast media must be managed under the Waste Control Regulation, Alta Reg 192/1996, with approved manifests and disposal records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and occupancy permit from the local fire authority; structural load inspections and certification by an Alberta-licensed Professional Engineer for overhead crane rails, berth structures, dry-dock gates and launchways; Occupational Health and Safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act and General Regulation, AR 174/2021, including a written site-specific emergency response plan, confined-space entry program and hazardous-material (WHMIS) inventory for shipyard premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online / My Business Account portal (www.canada.ca/taxes-business)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign shipyard entity must first obtain a nine-digit CRA Business Number (BN) via Form RC1 (Application for Registration) or through Business Registration Online if eligibility criteria are met. To collect, remit, or recover GST/HST, the entity must concurrently apply for a GST/HST program account (RT) on the same registration. For maritime goods crossing borders, an Import/Export (RM) account is required. Non-resident applicants must provide certified copies of foreign incorporation documents, a foreign registry extract, and proof of a Canadian representative (Form RC59). Approval is generally issued within 2–4 weeks, after which the entity receives the BN and program account confirmation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with Canadian-resident worldwide tax liability; no tax-exempt zone treatment and no pass-through eligibility for a standard Business Corporation; Alberta does not maintain a separate provincial sales tax but corporate income tax is administered by CRA under a federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no direct check-the-box election for corporate entities; CRA determines classification under domestic law and tax treaties. Applicable elections include: (i) corporate tax residence tie-breaker under the Canada-US and other treaties; (ii) capital cost allowance (CCA) and class elections under the Income Tax Act; (iii) rollover elections for amalgamations and asset transfers under sections 85, 86 and 87; (iv) GST/HST filing frequency election (monthly, quarterly, or annual); and (v) a voluntary GST/HST registration election for exporters to claim input tax credits. Hybrid mismatch and anti-arbitrage rules under section 18.4 apply automatically and cannot be overridden by an election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in combined annual taxable supplies in Canada for domestic persons; a non-resident carrying on business in Canada must register if Canadian-source taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and a shipyard exporter should nevertheless voluntarily register to claim input tax credits on purchases attributable to zero-rated export sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. GST/HST returns are filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or API-enabled commercial software on a periodic basis; invoices must contain prescribed information including vendor BN, HST registration identification, invoice date, and tax status. E-invoicing is permitted but not mandatory, and there is no pre-clearance API approval from the CRA for individual export invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported by the manufacturer directly to a non-resident are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. For ocean-going container vessels, zero-rating applies when the vessel is sold to a non-resident buyer and is either delivered into the buyer's foreign navigation or exported as part of the supply within 60 days; attendant services such as design, engineering, and offshore testing are zero-rated if performed wholly outside Canada or in direct respect of the exported vessel. The zero rate can be claimed only with contemporaneous export documentation demonstrating the physical export of the vessel and the non-residence of the purchaser.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13A)
Bill of Lading or equivalent ocean transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of receipt of foreign currency payment from the non-resident buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated supply to taxable status if the export documentation is incomplete or does not establish that the goods left Canada and the payment was received. Any denied zero-rating results in full collection of unreported GST/HST plus arrears interest. A false or negligent statement in support of an export zero-rating claim carries a gross negligence penalty of 25% of the amount assessed; fraudulent conduct may trigger criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. CRA retains a four-year normal reassessment window, but the period is unlimited where misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default is established. The exporter must retain all supporting export documents for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada maintains no general foreign-exchange-control statute: the former Exchange Control Act was allowed to lapse in 1951, and the Canadian dollar floats freely without central-bank conversion licensing or registration for individual foreign-exchange transactions. The Department of Finance Canada holds foreign-exchange policy responsibility; official international reserves are held in the Exchange Fund Account and managed by the Bank of Canada as fiscal agent. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises federally chartered banks; FINTRAC administers cross-border transaction reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); and Global Affairs Canada enforces economic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the United Nations Act, and export controls under the Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions, and Canada accepts IMF Article VIII obligations. There is no blocking of profit remittance, no non-convertibility approval requirement for dividends, loan repayments, royalties, or technical fees, and no obligation to obtain ministerial consent for operational remittances. The only statutory costs and conditions on outward remittance are: (i) Income Tax Act Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory, reduced to typically 5-15% under applicable tax treaties such as the Canada-US Convention); (ii) the corporate-law solvency test (ABCA/CBCA) that must be satisfied before a dividend or capital reduction is made; and (iii) standard CRS/FATCA beneficial-ownership self-certification and FINTRAC EFT reporting by financial intermediaries. Capital injections into a Canadian corporation from foreign shareholders are likewise unrestricted, subject to the Investment Canada Act review thresholds where the transaction involves acquisition of control rather than a subscription into an existing controlled entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, conversion ratio, or holding-period rule on export receipts. A Canadian shipyard may retain export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts in Canada or at offshore banks without restriction. The only associated obligations are (i) filing a Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export declaration (B13A) for goods exported above the prescribed reporting threshold; (ii) maintaining complete books and records of export transactions for income tax and customs audit; (iii) obtaining EIPA export permits where the goods are on the Export Control List (including certain dual-use or military-capable vessel designs); and (iv) automatic financial-institution reporting to FINTRAC of any cross-border electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, which is an AML/CFT intelligence measure and does not constitute a limitation on free disposition of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: CAD Commercial Operating Account; segregated USD sub-account; Escrow/Holdback sub-ledger for maritime installment deposits
Business Operating Account; controlled-borrowing and trade-service sub-limits; conditional escrow module for refundable advances
Commercial Operating Account with Trade Finance sub-limits; marine-receivables and documentary-credit desk
Commercial Account; non-cash facilities for LC issuance and standby guarantees; structured project account
Global Commercial Account; USD correspondent network over Fedwire/CHIPS; trade route strengths in Latin America and Asia
Commercial Operating Account / Trade-Centre account for Canadian-dollar payroll and domestic supplier payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury layer, and viable only as a secondary concentrate-and-disburse rail for low-value payments. A foreign electronic-money institution (EMI) such as Wise, Airwallex, or similar overseas-licensed providers may process B2B cross-border payments into Canada only if it is registered as a money services business with FINTRAC and, to the extent it provides payment functions to Canadian end-users, complies with the Bank-of-Canada-administered Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration regime. Foreign EMIs are not deposit-taking Canadian banks, cannot issue or receive documentary letters of credit, and cannot operate shipbuilding escrow accounts or maritime installment guarantees. A compliant structure is for the EMI to settle through API integration with a Tier-1 Canadian bank, but the shipyard's capital-injection, installment LC, and large trade-disbursement rails must remain at a regulated domestic bank. Feasibility rating: Medium for subcontractor payroll, refunds, and visa/expense reimbursements; Low for escrow, LC, and high-value term settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no Canadian statutory mandate that directors physically attend a bank branch. FINTRAC permits remote identity verification using either (i) a dual-process digital identity method or (ii) a verification service relying on a Canadian credit-bureau/identity database. In practice, Tier-1 banks onboarding a Medium_Risk_Enhanced marine manufacturer will require: an interactive video interview with the signing directors, corporate secretary, and ultimate beneficial owners; original or certified true copies of government-issued photo identification; corroboration through the Alberta Corporate Registry; and a bank-to-bank reference from any material counterparty bank. Non-resident directors may be onboarded by video meeting where they attend jointly with a resident Canadian signing officer, or with notarized and apostilled powers of attorney. A physical in-branch confirmation is generally imposed only for unusual ownership chains, third-party escrow structures, or where the beneficial owner is in a high-risk jurisdiction; otherwise remote opening is legally available and, in current Canadian practice, accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use and controlled-export exposure: commercial shipbuilding of deep-sea dry cargo and container vessels (ISIC 3011 / NAICS 336611) may implicate Canada's Export Control List and require EIPA permits; banks treat this as a possible military-capability or proliferation-financing red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EIPA end-use/end-user certificate or a written Global Affairs Canada classification opinion confirming a purely commercial cargo-vessel design; complete technical specification and hull drawings showing no military adaptation; classification-society certificates (ABS, DNV, Lloyd's Register); executed shipbuilding contract with the owner's civilian-operation undertaking; in-house export-control manual; real-time denied-party-screening log; attestation of a designated sanctions-compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-based enhanced due diligence: the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking-AML risk tier for heavy marine manufacturing, combined with high-value cross-border supplier flows, triggers enhanced underwriting scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the prior three complete fiscal years; board-approved two-year business plan with cash-flow and FX-exposure tables; executed shipbuilding contract, memorandum of intent, or owner's progress-payment schedule; supplier ledger covering twelve months with country-of-incorporation details; Alberta Corporate Registry extract; Transport Canada or recognized flag-state construction approvals; professional bios of directors and UBO attestations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media name matches: vessel flag, beneficial-owner nationality, charterers, or procurement jurisdictions touching SEMA/UN/OFAC-listed territories or state-owned enterprises may freeze account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer/vendor KYC files with adverse-media research packages; retained denied-party-screening results against bank sanction lists; end-user declarations signed by each major equipment supplier; certified PCMLTFA compliance-program attestation; post-delivery deployment confirmation that the vessel will trade only on free and non-sanctioned routes; written beneficial-owner representation setting out nil sanctioned-affiliation findings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and wealth scrutiny for large inbound capital injection: a non-resident equity subscription of substantial size into an industrial balance sheet triggers origin-of-funds review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent/ultimate-shareholder resolution authorizing the equity injection; subscription and share-issuance agreement; group organizational chart with UBO declarations; FATCA/CRS self-certifications for every controlling person; bank statements or an auditable transaction trail proving lawful accumulation of the remitted funds; undertaking to file Alberta share-issue records and to keep any back-to-back intercompany loan Part XIII-compliant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party instruction and escrowed refund-advance flags: stage payments from shipowners into a capital escrow account may present a 'conduit'/third-party misdirection or fraudulent-jurisdiction red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed shipbuilding contract with a fixed installment schedule (typically 10-40-40-10); escrow/stakeholder agreement naming the bank as disinterested escrow agent; irrevocable direction letters from the shipowner/beneficiary; invoice set tagged with one consistent project reference mirrored in SWIFT MT103 field 70 remittance information; complete UCP600 documentary-compliance pack for each installment draw.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pacs.008) from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the shipyard's CAD commercial operating account at a Tier-1 Canadian bank, settled in central-bank finality over Payments Canada LYNX (RTGS). No Bank-of-Canada exchange-control approval is required; the receiving bank requires the wire's remittance information to state 'share subscription / paid-in capital' (or 'intercompany loan' where debt-funding is used) and the originator's bank must identify the ultimate beneficial owner. The verification bundle consists of: board resolution authorizing issuance; updated Alberta share register; CRS/FATCA self-certifications for all UBOs; and an origin-bank reference. For wires of CAD 10,000 or more the receiving bank automatically files an Electronic Funds Transfer report with FINTRAC as an information-only AML measure. Funds may be retained in a USD sub-account without conversion; if conversion to CAD is elected, the treasury desk should pre-book a market-rate forward or spot transaction with the same bank to lock the rebalancing cost, using the bank's standard FX confirmation and settlement-risk controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails, in order of prevalence: (1) SWIFT MT103 supplier wires for discrete invoices covering steel plate, castings, marine engines, electrical switchgear, and subcontract works, each carrying the invoice number and project code in field 70; (2) commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700 series) with the presenting documents being commercial invoice, clean on-board bill of lading, insurance certificate, and inspection certificate, per the issuing bank's terms; (3) maritime installment LC or stage-payment escrow-release protocol driven by the shipbuilding contract milestones (keel laying, launch, delivery) and evidenced by classification-society progress certificates; (4) domestic CAD disbursements executed through Payments Canada ACSS/EFT, and through the Real-Time Rail where credit-risk terms permit; (5) USD obligations routed via the Canadian bank's US correspondent over Fedwire or CHIPS. Export Development Canada (EDC) may provide guarantees or receivables insurance to stretch supplier payment terms and secure pre-export working capital. All FX executed simultaneously with these payments is centrally netted under an ISDA/CSA relationship to reduce physical payment count and settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR forward contracts booked with a Tier-1 Canadian bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex
Cross-currency (USD/CAD) basis swaps matching long-dated USD export receivables against CAD operating liabilities

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing restricted-currency procurement pairs (e.g., USD/CNH, USD/INR, USD/KRW), permissible where physical delivery is legally inconvenient for the offshore counterparty
Plain-vanilla FX option collars and participating forwards to protect minimum margins while retaining upside on major contract awards
Listed exchange-traded FX futures and short-dated options for tactical, margin-efficient hedging of near-term payroll and supplier balances

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 21% M&P combined rate (13% federal manufacturing & processing + 8% Alberta) for qualified Canadian shipbuilding profits; federal Clean Technology Manufacturing Investment Tax Credit (30% refundable for eligible assets); Alberta Investment Tax Credit for manufacturing capital expenditures up to 10% for qualifying vessel construction equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return including Schedule 1 (Federal) and Alberta Schedule 4, filed electronically via CRA EFILE / My Business Account (mandatory for most filers; paper permitted only with explicit CRA concession).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File no later than 6 months after the corporation’s fiscal year-end; tax balance of 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations claiming the Small Business Deduction); Alberta instalments align with federal prescribed due dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide income from vessel construction, ship repair, design fees, and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident reports only Canadian-source business income attributable to a permanent establishment (PE) in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after deductions for cost of goods sold, labour, capital cost allowance, warranties, and GIFI expense allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses allocated on a separate-account basis to the Canadian PE; head-office overhead apportioned under Form T1122.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after non-capital loss carryovers and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses connected to the Canadian PE are deductible; foreign loss carryovers unavailable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal base tax at 15% (13% for qualified M&P profits claimed via the general rate reduction); subtracts foreign tax credits and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Federal rate applies to PE taxable income; treaty-based PE income protected through mutual agreement procedure on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial tax at 8% of Alberta taxable income, less provincial non-refundable and refundable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Alberta levy applies when a PE exists in Alberta; cross-border PE income apportioned under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing disclosure of reportable non-arm’s length non-resident transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000; includes methodologies and functional-cost allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for any non-arm’s length non-resident counterparty; failure to file triggers per-day fines and penalty exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay (max 12 months); repeated failures attract 10% + 2% per month (max 20 months). Interest at the CRA prescribed quarterly rate applies to late payments and instalments. T106/Schedule 88 non-filing: CAD 100 per day up to CAD 50,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding on dividends paid to non-residents; treaty-reduced to 5% for 10%+ corporate shareholders and 15% for portfolio shareholders (Canada-USA and most OECD treaty partners).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (i) execute and file CRA Form NR301 (or NR302/NR303 for partnerships) before payment; (ii) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US residents); (iii) if excess withholding occurred, apply for a refund via Form NR7-R within 2 years; (iv) retain TRC, treaty-entity declaration, and underlying shareholding certificates for audit; (v) file Form T1142 for distributions from foreign affiliates if applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 25% on interest and 25% on royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty-reduced interest: generally 0% for arm’s length dealings under Canada-USA and Canada-UK treaties; 15% for certain related-party participating interest under Canada-USA. Royalties: typically 10% under Canada-USA / Canada-Netherlands / Canada-Germany; 0% for certain copyright and patent information royalties where treaty protection applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate value of reportable transactions (T106/Schedule 88) with each non-resident related party; contemporaneous Local File / Master File documentation recommended when goods transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000 or services / interest / royalties / intangibles exceed CAD 500,000 per non-resident affiliate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s. 245) denies tax benefits from transactions lacking genuine economic substance, and treaty limitation-on-benefits clauses require demonstrable decision-making, personnel, risk retention, and premises within the Alberta shipyard.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false or misleading T2 return: inflating the cost of imported steel plates, padding vessel construction revenue, recasting personal expenses as corporate deductions, or channelling taxable shipyard profits into offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s. 239(1) and Criminal Code s. 380: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment up to 5 years; civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understatement under ITA s. 163(2); compounding interest on unpaid balances at CRA prescribed rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source withholdings, GST/HST, and related penalties under ITA s. 227.1; criminal conviction may result in travel bans, asset seizure, director disqualification under the CBCA, and extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterizing the price of intercompany procurements from non-resident affiliates (hull steel, propulsion systems, naval architecture licences) outside arm’s length ranges and failing to prepare contemporaneous documentation or file T106 / Schedule 88.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA re-determination under ITA s. 247(2) increases taxable income; penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment; interest on recomputed tax; loss of reliance on valuation ranges unless documentation is contemporaneous and demonstrates best-method use.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or approve materially false TP documentation expose the corporation to penalties and may be personally assessed for unremitted remittances; professional disciplinary exposure for signing certificates of compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a zero-tax conduit entity in a favourable treaty jurisdiction to hold vessel licensing royalties or shipyard shares without economic substance (no employees, premises, or decision-making) to fabricate eligibility for reduced withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under ITA s. 245 annuls the tax benefit and re-characterizes income; Part XIII deemed-dividend withholding of 25% imposed on indirect distributions; treaty benefits denied under limitation-on-benefits clauses; extended reassessment periods apply for misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability under tax-circumvention doctrines; knowingly executing false residency certificates constitutes forgery and can lead to imprisonment, permanent travel restrictions, and disqualification from corporate office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement a FINTRAC-required anti-money laundering program at the shipyard, failure to report suspicious transactions or large cash instalments exceeding CAD 10,000 in vessel payments, or accepting beneficial-owner financing through shell intermediaries without diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per first violation and CAD 2,000,000 for repeat violations; Criminal Code money-laundering charges (s. 462.31) carrying up to 10 years imprisonment; seizure and forfeiture of vessel, escort account, and shipyard assets; licence revocation under the Canada Shipping Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers are personally assessable for FINTRAC penalties; criminal conviction triggers asset-freezing orders, travel restrictions, and imprisonment; directors can be disqualified from public company board service.
